clue.text: Means buses can't move

indicators.note: the letters of the words that cannot move are made to move, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A complaint that the buses are stuck in traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges BUSESCANT; the apostrophe in 'can't' gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of substance has wealth, and means likewise refers to money or resources.

clue.text: Peg that is loose in Italian strings

indicators.note: the letters are let loose and fall into another order

explanation.surface: A tuning peg has come loose on an Italian stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges PEGTHATIS; 'strings' suggests violins but means long thin pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta comes in long thin strands, literally 'little cords' in the language of Italy.

clue.text: Flower trade improvement — there's money in it

indicators.note: the letter for money is placed in the word for a trade upturn

parts.note: a boom is a period of rapid economic growth
L, for libra, the pound sign

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside BOOM. L stands for the pound sterling, Britain's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloom is a blossom on a plant.

clue.text: They allow certain plants to get a firm hold

definitions.text: They allow certain plants to get a firm hold

parts.words: They allow certain plants to get a firm hold
parts.note: describes the thin coiling shoots with which climbing plants grip supports

explanation.definitionFit: Climbers like sweet peas send out coiling threadlike shoots that wrap around supports.

clue.text: Wine in the home? Most objectionable!

indicators.note: the wine goes in the word for a home

parts.note: a nest is a home, as in 'leave the nest'
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Drinking wine at home is deplored as most offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container: the Italian wine goes inside the word for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The nastiest thing is the most unpleasant or offensive.

clue.text: Able to bring parking into use

indicators.note: the letter for parking is brought into the word for use

parts.note: to exert strength is to use it

explanation.surface: Being able to find a use for a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is skilled, highly capable at something.

clue.text: Agree to strike

definitions.meaning: to be in harmony with it
a clock or bell sounding the hour does this

clue.text: The cost of an attack

definitions.meaning: a rush forward, as in a cavalry onslaught

explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a charge, and an onrush in battle is too.

clue.text: Being in command etc perhaps calls for a mental faculty

parts.note: taken as written
to tell someone to do something is to command them

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of etc might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Holding command and similar duties requires brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellect is the faculty of reasoning, a power of the mind.

clue.text: Duck in in the Schleswig- Holstein river

definitions.meaning: a large sea duck valued for its down
a river in northern Germany, once the Danish border

explanation.definitionFit: The sea duck prized for its down shares its name with a north German river.

clue.text: Swarms appearing since about spring

a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Insects swarm out once spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a leap; 'about' wraps the word for since around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that swarms is present in great numbers, teeming everywhere.

clue.text: The proposition Edward set out

explanation.surface: Edward lays out a proposal to the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: T' for 'the' is a northern English dialect form, as in 'down t' pit'. 'set out' is gardening: plants are set out in a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners say seedlings are set out or put in the ground in their final bed.

clue.text: Poet occupying a loft?

definitions.meaning: the ancient Greek epic poet of the Iliad
a racing pigeon kept in a pigeon loft is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad's author shares a name with a homing pigeon, a bird that lives in a loft.

clue.text: Not even one of the Baker Street boys

definitions.meaning: uneven, not regular in shape or pattern

definitions.text: one of the Baker Street boys
definitions.meaning: Sherlock Holmes's street urchins were called the Baker Street ...

explanation.walkthrough: Baker Street is where Conan Doyle's detective Sherlock Holmes lived in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven things lack uniformity; Holmes's band of street boys took this name.

clue.text: Taking rest, lies sprawling, so is never weary

indicators.note: the words lie sprawled untidily, so their letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lounging about resting claims that this is why they never get tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untiring keeps going and never gets weary.

clue.text: Felt better and got dressed again?

definitions.meaning: covered over once more, read literally as the answer

explanation.definitionFit: Getting well after illness, or being covered over once more, as a sofa is.

clue.text: Assistance for the man with a record

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
LP, a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man with an album offers support.

clue.text: Some crest! Some bird!

parts.note: a part is some of something
a ridge is a crest, as of a hill

explanation.surface: Two exclamations of admiration, at a hilltop and at a bird.

clue.text: A Roman Emperor's bloomer

a flowering plant whose root is used as a sedative

clue.text: Changing gear, give trouble

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a different order

clue.text: Starting in chiropody, treat only a part of the foot

definitions.text: only a part of the foot

indicators.note: the answer is the opening run of letters of the words in chiropody, starting them off

explanation.surface: Advice to a chiropodist beginning work: treat just a section of the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'foot' is the body part; the definition means the unit of length, of which an inch is a twelfth.
explanation.definitionFit: There are twelve inches in a foot measured as a length, so one is just a fraction of it.

parts.note: a quotation from Feste's song in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night with its last word missing, to be supplied

clue.text: Writing the hotel a note is quite natural

te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

clue.text: Start in error with the collection

clue.text: Risk coming by river

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
